newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan halts T-bill issue as has enough cash.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan halts T-bill issue as has enough cash.

text.p: Kazakhstan's ministry of finance said on Wednesday it would stop issuing treasury bills (GKOs) until next year as it had enough cash to cover its 1996 budget deficit from its $200 million Eurobond issued on Monday.

"Connected with this (Eurobond), the need to issue GKOs to cover the budget deficit has fallen," Daniyar Abulgazin, head of the Finance Ministry's treasuries department, told a news conference in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
He said the issue of three-month, six-month and 12-month state treasury bills would stop at least until the end of 1996.
The oil-rich republic's debut three-year Eurobond, organised by Dutch bank ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, was priced to yield 9.3 percent or 350 basis points above comparable U.S. Treasury notes.

According to the National Bank of Kazakhstan, the former Soviet republic's volume of GKOs totalled 13.7 billion tenge ($188 million) as of December 1. The yield on 14-day notes auctioned by the National Bank on Tuesday was 29.65 percent a year.
An economist with a major investment bank said the Eurobond has sparked great interest in Kazakh debt but added the young market's small volume was a limiting factor.
"I'm getting calls from clients everyday about the Kazakh market," the economist said. "But there's not much room for major investors when market volume only totals $200 million."
